name: GitLab feature-flags provider-local route (CHAOS-3702)
$limitation: Provider-local mutation coverage only. The focused route suite proves the valid multi-page request sequence, physical request accounting, scope rows, three destinations, cap/no-watermark, non-list fail-closed behavior, qualified 403 classification, plain-403 terminal dataset classification, invalid configuration guards, project fallback, recovery policies, result identity, and evidence identity. The fresh live proof executes the pinned Python client, normalizers, worker edge block, and real WorkGraphBuilder methods with a capturing sink. Frozen tests do not contain malformed nested scope shapes, project HTTP/decode failures, duplicate scopes with different timestamps, or sub-millisecond timestamp precision cases; those unmeasurable mutations are intentionally excluded rather than overstating coverage. This plan intentionally excludes registry, matrix, scheduler, transport wiring, ClickHouse implementation, and the mutation harness itself.

mutations.rationale: a nil context must fail closed before the provider client or any effect is reached
invalid leased claims must be rejected before provider I/O
a GitLab claim for another dataset must not be accepted by the feature-flags route
a missing resolved HTTP client must fail before dereference
the resolved client provider must agree with the claimed GitLab route
path construction requires a resolved base URL
a client without a request doer must fail closed before pagination
the route needs a nonzero observation instant for deterministic rows and watermark evidence
zero handler configuration must resolve to the production defensive page cap
zero handler configuration must resolve to the Python client's per-page default
nonpositive page caps must be rejected rather than silently disabling traversal limits
page traversal must reject a MaxPages value above the defensive bound
nonpositive per-page configuration must fail before a provider request
accepted fetch evidence must count every physical page and project request
the first physical requests must target GitLab's feature_flags endpoint exactly
the project GET must remain the second endpoint after all flag pages and use the same project scope
the physical GitLab query must report the configured per_page value used by the Python client
the route's explicit page cap must reach the shared paginator
a nonempty X-Next-Page header is authoritative for GitLab traversal

mutations.rationale: the provider route must emit feature_flag, feature_flag_event, and work_graph_edges together
normalized flag rows must target the feature_flag destination exactly
snapshot events must target the feature_flag_event destination exactly
captured identity/configuration edges must target work_graph_edges, with no LaunchDarkly link destination
feature_flag writes must retain their replay-safe recovery policy
feature_flag_event writes must require readback recovery
work_graph_edges are replay-safe and must not be changed to readback recovery
a complete successful collection must return the leased upper-bound watermark candidate
route result project_key must be the canonical project response/fallback, distinct from the claimed identifier when GitLab resolves a path
route result must preserve the exact claimed project id/path separately from the resolved canonical project key
fetch evidence must account for every physical flag-page and project request
fetch evidence must report all physical flag pages traversed
accepted evidence must include all three canonical output row families, including work_graph_edges
fetch evidence must retain the provider identity used by the route
fetch evidence must retain the canonical feature-flags dataset identity
a plain GitLab feature-flags 403 is an unavailable project dataset, while 401 and unrelated status classes must retain their credential or provider meaning
the endpoint-specific 403 must reach the provider-unit state machine as a durable unavailable-dataset verdict instead of consuming every River attempt as generic exhaustion
a deterministic feature-flags access denial must fail with provider_dataset_unavailable on the first attempt rather than re-entering dispatch and ending as provider_unit_exhausted
only the feature-flags inventory endpoint may translate a plain 403 into unavailable-dataset; the project-name lookup must retain ordinary authentication semantics
